fields.v: Task-conditioned assurance envelope, 'V1' of the formulation (author's own); implementation in Python with NetworkX and OR-Tools CP-SAT. Diagnostic baselines: ALL (retain every evidence leaf) and FLAT (AND rules projected into pairwise links + weighted set cover)

Task obligations ('roots') R(P,t,M) supplied by hand; typed evidence items (passing tests, type checks, discharged contracts, static analyses, monitored traces) with semantic type, context identifier, assumptions and integer cost; explicit inference rules forming a directed hypergraph (AND/OR); selected envelope S* with derivation provenance; canonical manifests. No specification artefact for code generation

Supply artifact P, task t and context M -> supply task roots R(P,t,M) and inference rules -> build typed inference graph G -> solve minimum-cost sufficient support (CP-SAT or exhaustive oracle) -> independent closure validation (forward chaining) -> envelope or explicit 'no sufficient envelope' report (Fig. 1). Envisioned: a long-horizon agent requests an envelope before modifying a component (not tested)
Not stated as review points; obligations and inference rules are hand-specified by the author ('This study supplies roots manually')
Single artefact / mechanism: evidence-selection step only, over frozen graphs; no coding agent consumes the envelope ('does not test whether a downstream coding agent performs better')
Not classifiable (assurance-evidence selection for supplied obligations; authors do not use SDD terms)

Feasibility/infeasibility of an envelope; closure validity of selected supports; FLAT false coverage (invalid task evaluations and false roots); agreement of CP-SAT with exhaustive oracle; optimality proved within 60 s

Automatic: exhaustive search and CP-SAT (one worker, seed 0, 60 s timeout), independent closure validator, NetworkX; deterministic SHA-256 generator; timing on Apple M1 Pro, one run per graph and method. Obligations, rules and costs hand-specified (manual) and prespecified before evaluation

No agent + model configurations; the unit is the selection method on frozen graphs. Success criterion stated by the author: closure validity, Eq. 1 ('Operationally, Eq. 1 is the acceptance criterion', p. 4), and minimum cost, Eq. 2. No criterion stated for solve time. (1) Provenance-derived graphs, COMPOSITIONAL (exact search): Rust C local cost 2, trace cost 3; Rust B local cost 2, trace infeasible (no sufficient envelope, correctly reported); IronBlocks unique optimum cost 2; Pong R0 cost 1, R1 cost 2; all supports closure-valid. Quality: works; cost: works (exact minimum). (2) Provenance-derived, FLAT: IronBlocks two cost-1 optima, both rejected by closure. Quality: does not work; cost: not judged (cheaper supports are invalid). (3) Benchmark, COMPOSITIONAL (CP-SAT): 234/267 proven optimal, 30 proven infeasible (all F7), 3 closure-valid but not proven optimal within 60 s; no support failed closure; median support reduction F1 0.50, F3 0.80, F5 0.50, F6 0.60, F8 0.50, F2/F4 0 (curves in Fig. 3 only); median solve time <20 ms at n=500 for every family (Fig. 4), but in the separate F3 sweep with 10 alternatives per target all three n=100 instances reached 60 s. Quality: works; cost: partly (3 optima not proven; solve time: no criterion stated by the authors). (4) Benchmark, FLAT: false coverage in 135/267 evaluations (3,765 false roots), all in conjunction families F2, F4, F6, F7 (every evaluation of those families), none in F1, F3, F5, F8. Quality: partly (valid only where no conjunction is required); cost: not judged. (5) Benchmark, ALL: retains all leaves (reference for the reduction metric). Quality: works (closure evaluated on all evidence); cost: no criterion stated by the authors for ALL (it is the reference, not a candidate for minimum cost). Exact oracle: 111/126 method-instance checks completed, all agreed with CP-SAT; 15 n=20 compositional checks timed out
fields.why: Verdicts partly rested on the extractor's reading: FLAT on the benchmark was 'does not work' although it was valid in 132 of 267 evaluations; ALL got cost 'does not work' with no criterion for it; the COMPOSITIONAL cost 'partly' mixed an unproven-optimality criterion with solve time, for which no criterion is stated. Numbers checked and kept
fields.doubt: Os veredictos de custo assumem a Eq. 2 (custo mínimo) como critério; para o tempo não há critério. Decide se FLAT no benchmark é 'partly' (válido em 132/267) ou 'does not work', e se ALL recebe veredicto de custo.

fields.v: Tasks: 7 hand-specified graph/task cases (Table 1) + prespecified, frozen synthetic benchmark (8 families F1-F8, 3 seeds, sizes 10-500, plus 15/20 exact-only). Compared: COMPOSITIONAL vs FLAT vs ALL. Baseline: ALL and FLAT (diagnostic, 'intentionally lossy'). Held constant: same graphs, costs, solver settings (one worker, seed 0, presolve, no hints, 60 s). Acceptance: independent closure check; exhaustive oracle for n<=20; mandatory gate of 21 n=10 instances. Repetitions: one run per graph and method (timing); a second run reproduced timing-free results. Human intervention: obligations and rules hand-specified before evaluation

COMPOSITIONAL always closure-valid; FLAT invalid in 135/267 evaluations (all in conjunction families), and on IronBlocks; support reduction vs ALL from 0 (F2, F4) to 0.80 (F3). No significance testing (deterministic, counts reported)

Distinguished FLAT from COMPOSITIONAL clearly (by construction: FLAT 'necessarily fails' on conjunctions). Repeatable: all 249 manifests regenerated byte for byte; timing-free results reproduced. Limitations stated: FLAT is one prespecified abstraction, not every non-compositional system; synthetic families may favour the phenomena studied; timing machine-specific, one run

Obligations and rules hand-specified and may be incomplete or too strong; costs do not measure real acquisition, context or risk; small provenance-derived graphs, synthetic instances up to 500 leaves, not industrial; does not test whether a coding agent performs better with the envelope; Pong evidence reconstructed. Open: automatic construction of task roots R(P,t,M), artifact-evolution invalidation, downstream agent benefit, multi-objective costs
